assertions.name: two-strand trace of a single sigma is the Markov z = q^3/(q^2+1)
tr_M(atom) = prod_i tr_2(p_i(sigma)) for A = 2, 3, 4 below 1e-55
L_pp, L_nn, L_pn = -log(z + d) reproduce the arc's 200-bit H_6 values
Jones of the closure is the product of the torus-link Jones over the chain

description: The Markov trace (convention D, 200-bit) of the full 3A-strand canonical atom word equals the product over generators of two-strand traces of the per-generator Hecke polynomials, to ~1e-59 at A = 2, 3, 4; Jones factorises over the chain on both branches. Reason: the closure is a linear connected sum (chain form), and multiplicative invariants are multiplicative under connected sum. Interface factors are z + d, so the arc's bond constants are -log(z + d) to 60 digits and the canonical L is exactly a sum over interfaces: the canonical closure carries no many-body binding by theorem. The arc's cumulants belong to the all-pairs bond model, which is not a chain.
caveats: Checked at A <= 4 (n <= 12) in CI budget; the identity is a theorem for every A given the chain form, which the chain probe verified through A = 12. A = 6 is the same computation on a longer run.
Says nothing about which non-composite closure would carry many-body binding, or whether one exists in the framework. It says the canonical chain cannot, and why.
